## Ex 4: Descriptive stats/visualisation

### 1.

```{r}
install.packages("palmerpenguins")
library(palmerpenguins)
head(penguins)
```

### 2.

```{r}
penguins %>% 
  filter(species == "Adelie") %>% 
  ggplot(
    aes(x = bill_len, y = bill_dep)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  labs(
    title = "Bill Length vs. Bill Depth for Adelie Penguins", 
    x = "Bill Length (mm)",
    y = "Bill Depth (mm)")
```

### 3.

```{r}
penguins %>% 
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(mean_bill_length = mean(bill_len, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_bill_length = median(bill_len, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_bill_length = sd(bill_len, na.rm = TRUE))
```

### 4.

```{r}
penguins %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g), 
               names_to = "feature",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ feature, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Boxplots of Penguin Features by Species",
       x = "Species",
       y = "Value")
```

## Ex 2: Using Functions to Package Code

### 1.

```{r}
# All tasks combined in one function.
pengu_property_plotter <- function(df, penguspecies, x_val, y_val) {
  if (!(penguspecies %in% c("Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"))) {stop(glue::glue("{penguspecies} haben wir leider nicht :("))}
  if (!(x_val %in% names(penguins))) {stop(glue::glue("Noch nie von {x_val} gehört! :("))}
  if (!(y_val %in% names(penguins))) {stop(glue::glue("Noch nie von {y_val} gehört! :("))}
  if (!is.numeric(df[[x_val]])) {stop(glue::glue("{x_val} ist wohl nicht numerisch! :("))}
  if (!is.numeric(df[[y_val]])) {stop(glue::glue("{y_val} ist wohl nicht numerisch! :("))}
  df %>% 
    filter(species == penguspecies) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = .data[[x_val]], y = .data[[y_val]])) + 
    geom_point() + 
    labs(title = glue("{y_val} vs. {x_val} for {penguspecies} Penguins")) 
    
}
pengu_property_plotter(penguins, "Adelie", "bill_len", "bill_dep")
```

### 2.

```{r}
# The function takes a data frame, penguin species, an x value and a y value. First it uses the given data frame and filters the column "species" for our given penguin species. It then plots a scatterplot given two columns that we assigned as the x and y variable. The title of the plot adapts to our chosen argument values.

```

### 3.

```{r}
# If we enter an invalid species, the plot is still formed, but the canvas is empty.
# If we enter en invalid x variable, the code fails
# If we enter a non-numeric column for the x variable the code still works and we recieve the distributions of the y variable for every category of the x variable.
```

### 4.

```{r}
# All tasks split up into smaller functions.
species_filter <- function(df, penguspecies) { 
  df %>% filter(species == penguspecies)
}

species_mapper <- function(df, x_val, y_val) {
  df %>% ggplot(aes(x = .data[[x_val]], y = .data[[y_val]])) + geom_point()
}

species_labeler <- function(x_val, y_val, penguspecies) {
  labs(title = glue("{y_val} vs. {x_val} for {penguspecies} Penguins"))}

species_filter(penguins, "Adelie") %>% 
  species_mapper("bill_len", "bill_dep") + 
  species_labeler("bill_len", "bill_dep", "Adelie")
```

## Ex 4: Recursion and Iteration

```{r}
fib_iterative <- function(power) {2 ^ power}
fib_iterative(30)

fib_recursive <- function(power) {
  previous_result <- 2 ^ (power - 1) 
  return(2 * previous_result)
}
fib_recursive(30)
```

## Ex 5: Refactoring

### 1.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(glue)
# Repetitions:
# Every species is handeled individually for both mean bill and mean mass.
# This also applies to the output, where every possible output is listed as an ifelse chunk.

# Distinct ideas:
# We want to choose a penguin species and recieve its mean bill length and mean mass

summarise_species <- function(species_name) {
  mean_bill <- mean(penguins$bill_length_mm[penguins$species == species_name], na.rm = TRUE)
  mean_mass <- mean(penguins$body_mass_g[penguins$species == species_name], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("Species:", species_name, "\n")
  cat("Length :", mean_bill, "\n")
  cat("Mass   :", mean_mass, "\n")
}
summarise_species("Gentoo")
```

### 2.

```{r}
penguin_report <- function(species_name) {
  
# Funktion 1: Laden und säubern des Datensatzes.
 pengu_loader_cleaner <- function() {
  library(palmerpenguins)
  library(tidyverse)
  pengu_data <- penguins
  pengu_data <- pengu_data[!is.na(pengu_data$bill_length_mm) & !is.na (pengu_data$body_mass_g),]
  return(pengu_data)
 }
 
# Funktion 2: Filter für den Datensatz, jetzt ist es für jede Species individuell.
 pengu_filter <- function(species_name) {
  filtered_data <- pengu_clean %>% filter(species ==   species_name)
  return(filtered_data)
 }
 
# Funktion 3: Zusammenfassung wichtiger Informationen für die gewählte Species.
  pengu_summariser <- function(species_name) {
   filtered_data <- pengu_clean %>% filter(species == species_name)
   summarised_data <- filtered_data 
   cat("Ausgewählte Species:", species_name, "\n")
   cat("n =", nrow(filtered_data), "\n")
   cat("mean bill length:", mean(filtered_data$bill_length_mm), "\n")
   cat("mean body mass:", mean(filtered_data$body_mass_g), "\n")
  }
  
# Funktion 4: Abbildung der gefilterten Daten in einem Streudiagramm
  pengu_plotter <- function(species_name) {
   filtered_data <- pengu_clean %>% filter(species == species_name)
   plot <- ggplot(data = filtered_data, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)) + 
    geom_point(color = "magenta") + 
    theme_dark()
    labs(title = paste("Bill length vs. body mass -", species_name))
   return(plot)
  }
  
# Jetzt werden alle Funktionen zusammengesetzt
  pengu_clean <- pengu_loader_cleaner()
  pengu_filtered <- pengu_filter(species_name)
  pengu_summariser(species_name)
  my_plot <- pengu_plotter(species_name)
  print(my_plot)
}

# Erfolgreicher Testversuch :)
penguin_report("Gentoo")
```

```{r}
library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)

mean_mass_by <- function(data, group_var) {
  data |>
    group_by(group_var) |>
    summarise(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE))
}

mean_mass_by(penguins, species)
# I expect this code to fail, because group_var is a function-specific variable and does not appear to be a column from the penguins data set, meaning there is no column that the observations can be grouped by.
```

## Ex 3: browser()

```{r}
my_factorial <- function(n) {
  stopifnot(n >= 0, n == as.integer(n))
  if (n == 1) return(1)
  return(n * my_factorial(n - 1))
}

my_factorial(5) 
```

## Ex 4: debug() and debugonce()

```{r}
standardise <- function(x) {
  (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

standardise(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5))   # fine
standardise(c(1, 2, NA, 4, 5))  # returns all NAs — why?
```
